messages:
Ava (frontend): noticed a spike on dashboard first-load in eu-canary — heatmap & timeseries paint much slower, main thread doing 150-400ms stalls on attach.
Ben (eng-platform): which deploy/PR? any recent bundler or telemetry changes?
Ava (frontend): seems tied to PR #2484 (telemetry client sampler rewrite) and the rollup upgrade to 2.7 (commit d3f7a2b). repro on eu-canary + qa env.
Jin (qa): repro steps I used: open dashboard with ~8 tiles, change range to last 7d, wait for streaming. saw big "Long Task" at first chart attach.
Ava (frontend): pasted quick logs:
```
[telemetry] sampler:init parsing blob size=95kb -> 140ms
[chart] attach start
[main] task 160ms at JSON.parse
```
Kai (telemetry): we moved sampler parsing to inline to save worker bundle size, but we do JSON.parse of the whole blob synchronously on init. that was an intentional change to reduce overhead but might be blocking.
Maya (sre): rolling canary back is an option if customers hit this. any quick mitigation?
Ben (eng-platform): grab a flame/profile from the repro and we'll iterate. If it's parse hotpath then revert sampler change temporarily.
Ava (frontend): uploaded a small trace -> shows JSON.parse dominating main thread on firstPaint and also duplicated telemetry chunk in the module graph (possible bundler dedupe regression after rollup bump).
Kai (telemetry): options: 1) move parse to worker 2) stream/ incremental parse 3) defer parse via requestIdleCallback or setTimeout after firstPaint.
Ben (eng-platform): immediate mitigation: can we lazy-init sampler after firstPaint? Ava, can you try setTimeout(() => initSampler(), 0) in canary and report?
Ava (frontend): testing setTimeout hack now in eu-canary. also will try requestIdleCallback in a parallel build.
deploy-bot: eu-canary deployment started (canary-weight 10%)
Jin (qa): running quick A/B — baseline vs setTimeout patch.
Ava (frontend): setTimeout reduced initial main-thread stall by ~70-80% in my QA runs. firstPaint improved ~120ms. requestIdleCallback similar but less consistent in Chrome headless.
Ben (eng-platform): good signal. I'll open an emergency PR to revert the sampler rewrite on canary and pin rollup to previous version if needed. assigning @ben and @kai to the revert + follow-up.
Kai (telemetry): follow-up plan: implement worker-based parse + streaming parser that incrementalizes JSON parsing, add e2e test asserting "no blocking long task > 50ms on firstPaint" and add telemetry size guard.
Maya (sre): created incident doc: https://redwood/ops/incident/heatmap-telemetry-blocking - tagging impacted canary customers.
Ava (frontend): leaving UX notes in the rollout ticket about noticeable jank and customer escalation. will add a small perf test in the dashboard smoke harness. :thumbsup:
Ben (eng-platform): also track bundler module graph — the duplication may be causing extra bytes parsed. Kai, can you verify if sampler bundle got duplicated after rollup bump?
Kai (telemetry): will investigate module graph and also run build with previous rollup to compare chunking/dedupe.
Ava (frontend): thanks team — reverting for now reduces customer impact. we'll schedule the worker + streaming parser in the next sprint and add guardrails in the console rollout flow.
Maya (sre): if revert PR passes canary, coordinate with support to notify the impacted accounts and close the incident doc.
Ben (eng-platform): PR #2540 opened to revert sampler rewrite on canary and pin rollup to 2.6. assigning reviewers.
Ava (frontend): verified PR #2540 test build — heatmap render back to baseline on eu-canary. will keep monitoring.
Kai (telemetry): long-term tasks: worker parse, size budget for telemetry payloads, build-time dedupe checks.
Jin (qa): adding a regression test to nightly that captures firstPaint long-tasks for dashboards with telemetry enabled.
Ava (frontend): thanks all, closing the loop here.
